title: AlertEvent
description: A discrete detection raised by a SIEM, EDR, IDS, or other detection source. Adapters must map vendor-native alert formats into this shape; see adapters/contract/adapter.schema.json.

event_class.description: Fixed discriminator so ClickHouse/Qdrant consumers and the agent's tools can dispatch on event type without inspecting every field.

uid.description: Globally unique ID for this alert, ideally the vendor's native alert ID prefixed with the adapter name (e.g. crowdstrike:abc123) for traceability back to source.

time.description: RFC3339 timestamp of when the alert fired, in the source system's clock — not ingestion time.

severity.description: Normalized severity. Adapters must map vendor-specific severity scales (e.g. Crowdstrike 1-5, Splunk urgency) onto this fixed set.

message.description: Human-readable alert summary as provided by the source, lightly normalized.

category.description: Free-text detection category from the source (e.g. 'malware', 'lateral-movement', 'credential-access'). Not constrained to a fixed enum at the canonical layer since taxonomies vary too much across vendors; used for search/filter, not strict typing.

mitre_attack_techniques.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs if the source provides mapping (e.g. T1055, T1003.001).

adapter.description: Which adapter produced this event, e.g. 'crowdstrike', 'splunk-hec'.

native_id.description: The alert's original ID in the source system, unprefixed.

host.description: Optional — not every alert is host-scoped (e.g. a network-level or identity-level alert may omit this).

raw.description: The original, unmodified vendor payload, preserved for forensic fidelity and for cases where the agent needs a field the canonical schema doesn't surface.
